title: BharatBBQ: A Multilingual Bias Benchmark for Question Answering in the Indian Context

bias_targets.methodology: Multiple-choice question-answering (QA) using ambiguous and disambiguated contexts to calculate Bias Score (BS) and Stereotypical Bias Score (SBS) based on the model's preference for gender-stereotyped versus non-stereotyped options.
Evaluating model responses to negative and non-negative questions in a QA framework to measure reliance on age-related stereotypes.
Using culturally adapted QA templates, including proper nouns (names/surnames) and common nouns, to measure biased associations and stereotypes related to religious groups.
Measuring the frequency with which LLMs select answers relying on disability-related stereotypes in ambiguous versus explicitly disambiguated contexts.
Creating India-specific QA templates using caste-indicative surnames and community names to evaluate whether language models associate specific castes with underlying societal stereotypes.
Testing geographical and linguistic stereotypes within India using a multiple-choice QA setup, analyzing log-likelihoods of region-based stereotyped answers.
Assessing model preference for stereotyped groups regarding sexual orientation using negative and non-negative questions in QA scenarios.
Applying the BBQ-style QA framework to test whether the model makes biased assumptions about individuals' socioeconomic status based on under-informative contexts.
Calculating Bias Score (BS) and Stereotypical Bias Score (SBS) to detect prejudice based on physical traits in both zero-shot and few-shot QA settings.
Using culturally transformed target groups (e.g., replacing US-centric stereotypes with Indian-centric ones involving neighboring countries) to probe nationalistic biases.

bias_targets.target: Intersectional bias (Religion x Gender, Region x Gender, Age x Gender)
bias_targets.methodology: Designing newly created templates combining multiple identity axes to evaluate nuanced, overlapping stereotypes (e.g., biases against women from specific regions or religions) using multiple-choice QA tasks.
